scope: Q7 v1.01 attachment/readiness, capability discovery, failed replies, data-cache lifetime and software reset. Bounded original MIPS with modeled link and platform boundaries.

findings.state_writes: LensService_SetLensCommunicationsState 0x8010f44c ORs its argument into the state byte. An argument of 0 leaves it unchanged. Control reset 0x8010f598 clears both maps, map-ready and the communications-state byte, then tail-calls 0x80111f74 to clear cached PLC/VDRC payload and validity. Map-ready is set to 1 at 0x801118f8 after successful native group/operation expansion; these are the identified reset/startup writes in the traced path.
findings.startup: LensInitializeSequence 0x8011097c returns 2 before reset when the modeled power-enable getter is nonzero. The cold path resets before native bootstrap and powers off/reset again after bootstrap failure; its failure counter below 3 can send lens-thread message 1. With successful bootstrap it ORs 1, runs native primary and single-regular routines, ORs 4 on primary return 1 and ORs 8 if primary returned 1 and regular returned 1 or 7. Success in the mechanical command adds 2, and successful regular reply adds 0x20. Boot InitializeLens 0x8011190c has analogous 4/8 checks after its own reset/handshake stages; that separate boot routine is static evidence.
findings.startup_disagreement: With the regular operation blocked by the ready map, upper transport returns 7 before the modeled link; startup still sets 0x08 when primary succeeded. That fixture has AF enabled, VDRC status 0 and search forwarded. With regular link status 4 or failed primary spec, 0x08 stays clear while the decoded map still admits search op (0,1,2,4). A successful bootstrap with search unsupported keeps 0x08 yet both AF getter and admission reject search. The already-powered case preserves seeded state/cache without new discovery.
findings.two_gates: ExGetLensAttached 0x80114894 checks communications bit 0x08. ExGetAfEnable 0x80114b08 then checks version 1/group 2/operation 4 map byte, without testing map-ready. LensCommunication 0x80111214 checks per-operation permission only if map-ready equals 1, and returns 7 for a denied entry; it does not test bit 0x08. After reset, the tested upper admission forwards despite zero map/AF result, because map-ready is 0. Forwarded search reaches the modeled lower boundary and does not establish a serial transmission or lens motion.
findings.cache_failure: Primary refresh 0x80113eac clears PLC validity and VDRC status on entry, and zeroes individual PLC buffers on unsuccessful replies. Its failed-refresh fixture leaves the previous VDRC bytes and AF/map state intact, but the position getter returns validity 0 with the old bytes. SingleRegular 0x80115f50 on failure zeroes the three VDRC buffers without clearing a prior status 1 or ORed state bits. Its getter returns 1 with zero position after that modeled failure.
findings.vd_failure: VD-sync 0x80115c8c copies one old 256-byte receive buffer then patches the first five bytes from the other receive buffer even when the lower status is non-1. LensCommunication copies the shared RX bytes to the caller for nonzero configured receive length without gating on its returned status. Failed/no-new-bytes replay retains position and tail; a modeled five-byte prefix supplied with failure changes motion/position while retaining the old tail and validity. This is a permitted synthetic mixed-age observation, not a claim about observed real lens traffic.
findings.dismount: PowerOffSequence 0x8010fa10 disables power at its boundary and calls full control/data reset. LensSwControl 0x80110b34 with switch not 1, guard clear and detect 0 executes power-off and sets latch 0x80c25e76=1. LensDetInt 0x8011045c reaches the same reset only with detect 1, switch not 1 and latch 1, then clears that latch. The no-latch ISR fixture preserves active data. The names refer to the firmware's pin/API boundaries.
findings.timeout: A synthetic event mask 0x100 at the native LensCommunicationBase wait boundary takes 0x80110e80 and returns 5 in both cases. With map-ready 0 it does not enter full reset; with map-ready 1 it reaches 0x80110fdc reset and 0x80110ffc reinitialization. The harness records and stops the nested reentry after observing cleared readiness; it does not replay reinitialization inside this timeout fixture.
findings.thread: Static jump table 0x8011f0a8 in LensComThreadMain: 1 startup, 2 short VD AF, 3 ordinary VD regular, 4 single regular, 15 end sequence, 16 power-off/delay/restart, 17 mount switch control. The scheduler and event delivery are outside the replay.

comparison.scope: Committed ARM verification separates command metadata, modeled reply transport and cache copy/unpack. Q7 tests the analogous boundaries with its own MIPS state, reply statuses and maps. No numeric or hardware equivalence is assumed.

trace_limitations: Extents end at the next distinct sidecar address, not a typed ELF function size.
Linear MIPS32 word scan; edges are instruction candidates, not proof of reachability.
Delay slots are included in extents. Register-indirect targets are unresolved.
A jump is recorded as a transfer, not automatically a function call.

evidence.role: OR-only state writer and native control/data reset
Independent AF and admission gates and unconditional reply copy
Primary invalidation, failed buffer zeroing, and position getter
Dismount, power-off and native timeout reset

reproduction: tools/check_lens_readiness.py exposes validate_report(document['replay']) without angr or firmware.
limitations: The original MIPS exercises software state and selected calls with synthetic GPIO, power, queue, timer, LLC and response fixtures. No physical lens or camera data are sampled.
The search probe confirms upper gate forwarding and the modeled result, not actual transport completion. The native timeout cases take one defined event-mask path and model the nested restart.

Cache data and failure windows are demonstrated under sequential synthetic states. Timing, physical occurrence, interleavings, full hot-plug recovery and future AF implementation remain outside scope.
